name: liblaxjson
documented_input_api: lax_json_create(); lax_json_feed(context, int size, const char *data); lax_json_eof(context), with string/number/primitive/begin/end callbacks (include/laxjson.h, README usage)

popularity.metric: Debian popcon sourcemax installations, source package liblaxjson

probe: Throwaway event printer compiled with clang against the pinned laxjson.c in the pinned ubuntu base image (linux/arm64); it fed each valid control in one lax_json_feed call, then lax_json_eof, and printed each callback. Not committed as a project.

controls/json/nested-object.json.result: rejected: lax_json_feed returned 'unexpected character' at the value -0.25e1 of member "ratio", after delivering name, version (as double 1) and the ratio key
controls/json/nested-object.json.cause: LaxJsonStateNumberExponentSign accepts only '+' or '-' after 'e'/'E'; RFC 8259 makes the exponent sign optional. An exponent is also accepted only after a fraction part.

controls/json/nested-array.json.result: accepted with the full event sequence, but the integer 1 arrives as the double 1 through the only number callback, int (*number)(context, double); 2.5e-1 arrives as 0.25
controls/json/nested-array.json.cause: laxjson.c converts every number with atof() and has no integer callback or retained literal, so the cell's order- and number-kind-preserving oracle cannot be satisfied without the harness reinterpreting the source text.

decision: Not selected. The nested-object control fails, and number kinds are not observable on either control. With 1 Debian installation it also has the weakest possible positive signal. It stays a lead with this evidence; the tenth C JSON slot is left open.
scope: Valid controls only; no malformed-input, resource-use or fuzzing experiments.
